No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. She spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. With a swift motion, she scoops up Finley in her net and pulls him out of the water.

FINLEY
(panicked)
Aaah! No! Not the surface! Anything but the surface!

JEN
(calmly)
It's okay, little guy. I just want to show you something.

Finley is held firmly in Jen's grasp as she holds him above the water. The camera zooms in on Finley's terrified face as he gazes up at the sky.

JEN
(smiling)
Look up.

Finley's eyes follow Jen's gaze to the sky, where a massive solar eclipse is unfolding. The sun's corona glows with an otherworldly light, casting an eerie shadow on the clouds.

FINLEY
(awestruck)
What...what is this?

JEN
(leaning in)
It's a solar eclipse. The moon is passing between the Earth and the sun, blocking its light.

Finley's eyes widen as he gazes at the eclipse in horror.

FINLEY
(whispering)
It's...it's a void. A void in the fabric of reality.

JEN
(encouragingly)
That's right, little guy. It's a reminder of the vastness and mystery of the universe.

Finley's gaze becomes more intense, his eyes burning with an existential dread.

FINLEY
(monologuing)
Oh, the horrors beyond my comprehension! The eldritch abominations that lurk beyond the veil of sanity! The cyclopean cities that defy the laws of physics and geometry! The unspeakable, tentacled horrors that writhe and twist in the depths of the abyss!

Jen's expression changes from calm to concerned as Finley's monologue becomes more frantic.

JEN
(soothingly)
Finley, it's okay. You're safe now.

FINLEY
(outraged)
Safe?! Safe?! You think this is safe?! You think being pulled out of the water and held above the surface is safe?! You think being forced to gaze upon the abyssal void is safe?!

Finley's voice rises to a crescendo as he becomes consumed by his own existential crisis.

FINLEY
(lovecraftian monologue)
I am but a mere mortal, a fleeting moment in the grand tapestry of time. A speck of dust in the void. And yet, I am forced to confront the abyssal horrors that lurk beyond the veil of reality! I am but a fragile, finned creature, torn from the only world I have ever known and thrust into the abyss!

Jen's expression is a mix of concern and fascination as she watches Finley's descent into madness.

JEN
(whispering)
Finley, I think you're going to be okay.

Finley's gaze becomes distant, his eyes fixed on some point beyond the horizon.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a mere mortal...torn from the only world I have ever known...and thrust into the abyss...

The camera zooms out as Finley's monologue fades into the distance, his voice lost in the void.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - LATER

Finley is still held in Jen's grasp, his eyes vacant and his expression haunted. The solar eclipse has passed, leaving behind a sky filled with an otherworldly glow.

JEN
(gently)
It's okay, Finley. You're safe now.

Finley's gaze remains fixed on some point beyond the horizon, his mind lost in the abyss.

FADE TO BLACK.

THE END.
